A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' similarity-conditioned Mixup research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E in v1 and A–J in v2 are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and renaming.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR classification, Airfoil and time-series regression, similarity ablation, cross-validation, and training-time results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original repeated-run classification and regression experiments, toy-data demonstrations, ablations, and timing measurements. These are distinguishable from the externally attributed baseline scores in Table 2.

M1.justification: The central coefficient-generation procedure changes: v1 uses Beta-CDF warping with a kernel increasing exponentially with distance; v2 uses inverse-Beta-CDF warping with a distance-decreasing Gaussian kernel (Sections 3.2–3.3). v2 also fixes initial coefficients to uniform/Beta(1,1), removing tunable alpha. Separate input/target warping remains available in Appendix G.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet classification evaluations and Moons/Circles toy classification experiments. CIFAR10/100, Airfoil, Exchange-Rate, and Electricity remain. Coverage therefore expands substantially into larger-scale image classification and explicit non-convex toy problems.

E2.justification: v2 adds reproduced classification comparisons with RankMixup and Manifold Mixup, plus attributed calibration baselines including MMCE, ECP, LS, FL, FLSD, CRL, CPC, and MbLS (Table 2). Regression adds RegMixup (Table 4). MIT-L disappears, and v1's ResNet34 RegMixup/MIT comparisons are absent from the corresponding v2 Table 1.

E3.justification: The stated CIFAR learning-rate decay epochs change from 100/150 to 80/120. v2 adds ResNet101 comparisons, AECE, and distinct Tiny-ImageNet/ImageNet training protocols. New analyses introduce distance-quantile controls, before/after temperature-scaling measurements, and validation-selected best-epoch timing. These establish reported protocol changes without establishing which retained numerical results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's hyperparameter heatmaps and similarity ablation, v2 adds manifold-intrusion cases, controlled distance-quantile mixing, direct versus lookup-table sampling comparisons, and Airfoil warping-function and similarity-space analyses (Section 3.1; Appendices D, G, J). Hyperparameter sensitivity is revised, while v1's classification-weight and asymmetric input/target similarity comparisons disappear.

E5.justification: v2 reports ten runs for all regression datasets, versus five for Exchange-Rate/Electricity and ten for Airfoil in v1. Classification retains four runs and standard deviations. v2 additionally specifies averaging cross-validation over four splits and reports uncertainty for implementation timing in Table 7, whereas v1's timing table contains single values.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, ablation, and timing results; ImageNet results include 76.2±0.26 accuracy and 1.46±0.09 ECE (Table 3). v1's Airfoil Beta-CDF MAPE of 1.694±0.176 reappears in v2 Table 9 alongside the inverse-CDF variant's 1.609±0.137. Earlier ResNet50 CIFAR benchmark results and most RMSE baseline entries disappear. Revised methods and settings preclude treating these additions as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 revises the central mathematical definitions of the warp and similarity kernel and adds Proposition 3.1 with its Appendix F proof: inverse-CDF warping transforms a uniform coefficient into an exact Beta(tau,tau) variable. v1 instead illustrates approximately Beta-shaped outputs without this formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains efficient, similarity-conditioned Mixup improving performance and calibration across classification and regression. v2 adds an explicit main claim linking mixing distance to manifold-intrusion risk and extends efficiency claims to reaching the best validation performance faster, while emphasizing the accuracy–calibration trade-off.

C2.justification: v2 develops a substantive interpretation connecting distant mixing, non-convex manifolds, label noise, and calibration (Section 3.1). It replaces v1's dataset-dependent joint-hyperparameter explanation with a tau_std-dominated tuning account. Appendices B, I, and J add limitations concerning calibration theory after temperature scaling, hyperparameter selection, and explanations of warping and similarity choices.

D1.justification: Appendices G–I add GPU sampling and lookup-table implementation details, baseline hyperparameters and C-Mixup bandwidths, explicit stratified 90/10 cross-validation, and settings for the new datasets. The code reference changes from torch-uncertainty to a dedicated sim_kernel_mixup repository. Conversely, v1's averaging over the last ten classification epochs is no longer specified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands calibration-focused positioning through a dedicated calibration-driven Mixup discussion, RankMixup and calibration-regularization references, and detailed distinctions from AdaMixUp and Local Mixup. The offline oversampling subsection and references such as Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN are removed. These are substantive positioning changes beyond bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the abstract, contributions, related work, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The method narrative is reorganized around manifold intrusion; detailed settings and input/target disentangling move into appendices. Existing appendix material is reorganized alongside dedicated proof, implementation, sensitivity, and limitations sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds toy decision-boundary plots and distance-comparison boxplots, combines revised warp curves and density visualization in Figure 4, and replaces cross-validation heatmaps with tabulated sensitivity results. Classification and regression tables use reorganized dataset columns, timing expands into a multipart display, and the title, headings, typography, and page layout are redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces v1's approximate distribution argument with an exact sampling construction and proof. Controlled distance and warping analyses directly test previously weakly supported design assumptions, while broader calibration comparisons and detailed implementation settings substantially strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of some earlier ResNet50 and RMSE comparisons. Calibration itself remains unproved, but Appendix B now explicitly acknowledges that limitation.
